cards.explanation: The answer is that they rebelled against His law. The eagle looms "…because the people have transgressed My covenant and rebelled against My law." The reason comes right along with the warning, so nobody has to guess. When the horn blows, friends, God has already told them why.

The answer is False. Israel says, "…we know You!" and God answers, "…Israel has rejected good…" Then He adds that "an enemy will pursue him." Saying the words and holding on to the good are two different things, friends.

The answer is that they did it without His approval. God says, "They set up kings, but not by Me. They make princes, but without My approval." Israel handled the crowns on its own and left God out of it. Picture someone running your whole bakery schedule and never once asking you.

The answer is idols, friends. "With their silver and gold they make themselves idols, to their own destruction." They spent the good stuff on things that couldn't help them. Silver and gold went in, and idols came out. That's like pouring your whole paycheck into a toaster that doesn't toast.

The answer is True. God says, "For this thing is from Israel—a craftsman made it, and it is not God." So the calf came from a craftsman, not from God. Something somebody made can't be the One who made them.

The answer is False. God says, "It will be broken to pieces, that calf of Samaria." There's no "standing for years" in that sentence. A thing a craftsman made can be broken, and God says this one will be.

The answer is that foreigners would swallow it up. "Even if it should produce, the foreigners would swallow it up." First the grain doesn't stand and the sprouts give no flour. And if something does come in, outsiders take it anyway. Talk about no good news at the end of the row.

The answer is Assyria. "For they have gone up to Assyria like a wild donkey on its own." The verse compares Israel to a wild donkey on its own, and the place they go up to is Assyria. I think a donkey who wanders off alone is a picture you can't forget, friends.

The answer is True. God says, "Though they hire allies among the nations, I will now round them up…" They paid for friends among the nations, and God still says He will round them up. The hired help can't change that.

The answer is strange. "Though I wrote for them the great things of My law, they regarded them as something strange." God wrote them out, and Israel regarded them as something strange. I think that stings.

The answer is False. God says, "Though they offer sacrifices as gifts to Me, and though they eat the meat, the LORD does not accept them." They bring the gifts and eat the meat, but the LORD does not accept them. After that He says He will remember their iniquity and punish their sins.
The answer is Egypt. God says, "They will return to Egypt." That comes right after He says He will "…remember their iniquity and punish their sins…" The word "return" is right there in the verse.

The answer is fire. God says, "…I will send fire upon their cities, and it will consume their citadels." Israel built palaces and Judah multiplied its fortified cities. Walls and palaces look strong, but the verse says fire will consume the citadels.
